advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a voter-level test that clones a tree whose HEAD differs from the voted revision, and assert the voter casts NO vote (g.votes empty) and returns status=error / stage=reviewed_tree_mismatch.
evidence: The only new voter-level test asserts the happy path: `assert res["status"] == "voted"` / `assert g.votes and g.votes[0][1] == change_sha` (test_review_bot.py:1976-1978)
`CloningGerrit.clone_change_ref` always copies `self._change_repo` whose HEAD equals the voted `change_sha` — it can only produce a MATCH, never a mismatch (test_review_bot.py:1947-1954)
search of tests for `reviewed_tree_mismatch` returns no matches; `ReviewedTreeMismatch` appears only in adapter-level held-out tests, never at the voter seam
advisory.finding: The voter's new ReviewedTreeMismatch refusal path (voter.py:609-624) — casting NO vote and returning stage 'reviewed_tree_mismatch' — is never tested end-to-end. All voter-level coverage exercises only the matching/happy path; no test drives the voter with a clone whose HEAD differs from the voted revision to assert the voter refuses to vote and returns the mismatch stage.
scenarios: A regression where the voter swallows ReviewedTreeMismatch and casts a -1, or where the returned stage/status changes, would not be caught by any test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `CloningGerrit` variant (or reuse it with a change_repo whose HEAD != the event revision) and run `voter.review_and_vote`, asserting `res["stage"] == "reviewed_tree_mismatch"`, `res["status"] == "error"`, and `g.votes == []`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_binding_is_checked_before_any_review_work actually verify ordering by monkeypatching the gate entrypoint to append to `called`, so `called == []` fails if any review work runs before the mismatch raise.
evidence: `called: list[str] = []` (line 125) and `assert called == []` (line 131) with no code appending to `called` anywhere in the test
docstring claims 'Proven by the absence of any gate import/call on the mismatch path' but no gate function is monkeypatched to record into `called`
The only assertion with real content is `pytest.raises(adapter.ReviewedTreeMismatch)` — the `called == []` check is inert and would pass even if review work ran before the mismatch raise
advisory.finding: test_binding_is_checked_before_any_review_work asserts on a list that is never mutated, making the assertion vacuous: `called: list[str] = []` is declared but nothing ever appends to it, so `assert called == []` is trivially always true and proves nothing about the 'binding checked before any review work' contract the docstring claims.
scenarios: A refactor that moved `_assert_reviewed_tree` AFTER the gate import/invocation would still pass this test, defeating its stated purpose.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch the lazily-imported gate/review function to `called.append(...)` (raising=False if imported lazily), so the assertion `called == []` genuinely fails when review work precedes the raise.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 260 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug da31-f9d1-a81d-448c has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan da31-f9d1-a81d-448c` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review da31-f9d1-a81d-448c` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan da31-f9d1-a81d-448c --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
